# [Baseline] - AND - U - Work Profile Restrictions

On a device with a personal work profile, sets a separate work profile code (six digits, medium complexity, locks after fifteen minutes, wipes only the work profile after ten attempts), blocks copying, sharing and screenshots from work to personal, and turns on Play Protect.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Android |
| Scope | User (U) — assign to user groups |
| Type | Device config |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | UniFy Android Enterprise Baseline v1.5.1 — AND - DC - DR - USR - Personal-Work-Profile - v1.5; without password expiry, contact and caller ID blocks, account block and blocking of unknown sources on the personal side; lock time 15 instead of 5 minutes, the same as Compliance Password |
| File | [`Baseline_AND_U_Work_Profile_Restrictions.json`](Baseline_AND_U_Work_Profile_Restrictions.json) |

> Deliberately not adopted from UniFy: `workProfilePasswordExpirationDays` (365 — NIST SP 800-63B advises against rotation), `workProfileBlockCrossProfileCallerId` and `workProfileBlockCrossProfileContactsSearch` (break the name display for an incoming work call in the personal phone app), `workProfileBlockAddingAccounts` and `workProfileAccountUse: blockAll` (can cause adding the work account in apps to fail, UniFy W-6), `workProfileBlockPersonalAppInstallsFromUnknownSources` (a requirement on the personal side; Compliance Device Health already checks unknown sources), `workProfileBlockNotificationsWhileDeviceLocked` (App Protection already hides organisation data in notifications) and `blockUnifiedPasswordForWorkProfile` (see Compliance Password). `requiredPasswordComplexity: medium` at device level is a requirement on the personal side, but the same one that Compliance Password and App Protection already impose — without this line the user is not prompted to set it and simply becomes non-compliant. Two fields (`requiredPasswordComplexity`, `workProfileRequiredPasswordComplexity`) are not in the pl4nty definitions but are in UniFy's Graph export; on Android 12+ they are the ones that apply, length and type only on older versions.
